note: P6-04a BigInt division baseline. Measurement only, no production change.
head: dbb4391a
conclusion: cost is determined by the numerator's bit length alone; about 2.5 allocations per numerator bit; divisor width and normalization shift are both nearly irrelevant, exactly the shape of a bit-by-bit shift-subtract loop
current_implementation: src/libs/bigint.zig:533 divRemAbsAlloc walks the numerator one bit at a time: shl the remainder (one allocation), optionally addSmallInPlace, and on a subtract step subAbsAlloc (another allocation) plus setBit on the quotient
qjs_reference: js_bigint_divrem / mp_divnorm: normalize the divisor, estimate one quotient digit per limb, multiply-subtract with bounded correction

dynamic_topology.method: gdb silent breakpoints, slope between N=1 and N=21

laws.alloc_per_op: about 2.5 x numerator bits, independent of divisor width

dynamic_topology.contrast: after P6-03c a multiplication is 1 allocation per op, matching qjs; division is O(numerator bits) where qjs is O(1)

direct_core_size_matrix.harness: bigint/div-size-AxB and bigint/mod-size-AxB, zjs-only, median of three
direct_core_size_matrix.reading: the axis is numerator bits, not divisor width: 8x1 and 8x8 differ by 10% while 8x4 and 16x8 differ by 2.5x. div and mod cost the same because both call divRemAbsAlloc and discard one half.
direct_core_size_matrix.construction_note: the matrix saturates the numerator's top limb. Without that the lhs < rhs relation fell out of the pseudorandom pattern and 16x16 measured the early return at 31 ns against 8x8's 10 us.

normalization_shift_axis.reading: spread under 5% with no trend: the current algorithm never normalizes, so this axis is inert today. It is recorded now precisely because Algorithm D's qhat estimate depends on normalization, so the axis becomes live in P6-04c and the baseline will already have been measured on it.

rows.note: quotient 1 remainder 0, still walks all 256 bits

relation_axis.reading: eq and q1 are indistinguishable, so the cost is independent of the quotient's magnitude and depends only on the numerator's length

js_cross_engine.discrepancy_with_first_report: the earlier 306x / 283x used operands with a close to b (quotient 1, but still walking the whole numerator); this matrix saturates the numerator so it is strictly larger. Both are real, different shapes; later verdicts use these four cases.

criteria_for_p6_04b_and_c.p6_04b_single_limb_divisor: target shapes 2x1 / 8x1 / 16x1: shl per op should fall from 128 / 512 / 1024 to zero and alloc per op from 320 / 1273 / 2541 to O(1)
criteria_for_p6_04b_and_c.p6_04c_multi_limb: target shapes 4x2 / 8x4 / 16x8, and the sN axis becomes live
criteria_for_p6_04b_and_c.regression_sentinels: eq and q1 should collapse toward lt's magnitude under a limb-wise implementation; under the bit loop they cost the same as exact

limits: the direct-core matrix is zjs-only, like the multiply size matrix; cross-engine numbers come only from the four JS cases
setBit and addSmallInPlace have no separate symbols in the zjs binary (inlined), so their individual call counts are not broken out; they are included in alloc per op
alloc per op is not decomposed into shl / subAbsAlloc / setBit shares
negative operands and division by zero are not measured here; they belong to the correctness gate
pow is not measured; it repeatedly calls mulAlloc and is unrelated to division
